props.gloss_en: the mishna: one may not do hamra'a [to an animal on Shabbat]
Rav Yehuda: hamra'a is [placing food] into a place from which the animal cannot bring it back
Rav Yehuda: halata is [placing food] into a place from which it can bring it back
Rav Chisda: both are into a place from which it cannot bring it back; hamra'a is with a vessel
Rav Chisda: halata is by hand [into a place from which it cannot bring it back]
one may mehalketin chickens, and needless to say malkitin; one may not malkitin dovecote doves or attic doves, and needless to say not mehalketin
these [chickens], their sustenance is on you; those [doves], their sustenance is not on you -- so even throwing food before the doves is not permitted
one places food before a dog but not before a pig; the difference: this one's sustenance is on you, that one's is not
the mishna: one does not put water before bees or dovecote doves, but one does before geese, chickens and hardisian doves
R' Yona: the Holy One knows the dog's food is scarce, therefore its food stays in its innards three days
R' Yona: that is the meaning of 'the righteous knows the cause of the poor' (Prov 29:7)
the mishna: how long does its food stay in its innards and remain impure? for a dog three full days; for birds and fish, as long as it takes to fall into fire and burn
Rav Hamnuna: it is proper conduct to throw a piece of meat to a dog
Rav Mari: how much? the measure of its ear, and a stick after it
this applies in the field, but not in town, for it will come to follow [him]
Rav Pappa: there is none poorer than a dog and none richer than a pig
hamra'a: one lays it down, forces its mouth open and feeds it vetch and water at once; halata: one feeds it standing and waters it standing, vetch separately and water separately
